title: Design Database Scaling for ASP.NET Core Applications
description: Scale data access with read replicas, sharding, CQRS, and connection pooling in EF Core.

data.text: Your application has 100k concurrent users. The primary database is saturated. Design data access patterns that scale without compromising data integrity.
Route read-heavy queries to replicas. Keep writes on the primary. Works well when reads vastly outnumber writes.

data.title: EF Core with Read Replicas

data.text: Command Query Responsibility Segregation uses separate models for reads and writes. Reads can use denormalized views or document stores.

data.title: CQRS Pattern

data.text: Connection Pooling and EF Core Performance
EF Core adds overhead. Minimize it with connection pooling, compiled queries, and batching.

data.title: EF Core Performance Tips
items: Use compiled queries for frequently executed queries

data.title: Compiled Query Example
Scaling Read-Heavy Systems
data.text: Most web applications are read-heavy. Separating reads from writes using read replicas or CQRS gives you the biggest scaling win with the least complexity.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Read replicas distribute query load away from the primary
CQRS optimizes reads and writes independently
EF Core performance depends on tracking behavior and query shape
Compiled queries eliminate LINQ translation cost on repeated calls
data.takeaway: Database scaling is often the bottleneck. Combine read replicas, CQRS, and EF Core optimizations to handle high-throughput ASP.NET Core applications.
